entries.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
entries.whyTime: Binary search runs on the shorter array to find the partition, halving its range each step. That takes O(log(min(m, n))) steps.
entries.whySpace: Only the pointers and the partition values are stored, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
entries.whyTime: Each of the 2n − 1 centers expands outward while the characters match, up to n steps each. Time is O(n²).
entries.whySpace: Only the center and the best bounds are stored, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Zigzag Conversion
entries.whyTime: Each of the n characters is appended to one row bucket in a single pass, then the rows are joined. Time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The row buckets together store all n characters, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Reverse Integer
entries.whyTime: Each loop step strips one decimal digit, and a value n has about log n digits. Time is O(log n).
entries.whySpace: Only a few integers are stored, so space is O(1).

entries.title: String to Integer (atoi)
entries.whyTime: One scan skips the whitespace, reads the sign, then reads digits until the first non-digit. Each of the n characters is read at most once, so time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the index, the sign and the running number are stored, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Regular Expression Matching
entries.whyTime: The DP has a state for each prefix of s and each prefix of p, (m + 1)·(n + 1) states, each filled in O(1). Time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The table stores one value per state, (m + 1)·(n + 1) in all, so space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
entries.whyTime: Each of the n nodes is pushed into and popped from a min-heap of at most k nodes. Each heap operation costs O(log k), so time is O(n log k).
entries.whySpace: The heap holds at most one node from each of the k lists, so space is O(k).

entries.title: Reverse Nodes in k-Group
entries.whyTime: Each group is counted and then reversed, so every node is touched a constant number of times. Time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: Next pointers are rewired in place with no recursion, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence
entries.whyTime: KMP builds a prefix table over the needle in O(m), then scans the haystack once without moving back, in O(n). Time is O(n + m).
entries.whySpace: The prefix table stores one value per needle character, so space is O(m).

entries.title: Multiply Strings
entries.whyTime: Every digit of num1 is multiplied by every digit of num2, m·n products, each added into a result slot in O(1). Time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The result digits live in an array of m + n slots, so space is O(n + m).

entries.title: Rotate Image
entries.whyTime: Transposing visits about half of the n² cells, then reversing each row visits n² cells again. Time is O(n²).
entries.whySpace: Both steps swap cells in place, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Pow(x,n)
entries.whyTime: Each loop step squares the base and halves the exponent, so there are about log n steps. Time is O(log n).
entries.whySpace: Iterative: only the base, the exponent and the result are stored, so space is O(1).

entries.title: N-Queens
entries.whyTime: One queen goes in each row, and the column and diagonal sets skip clashing squares, so each row offers fewer columns than the last. The search tree has O(n!) nodes.
entries.whySpace: The column and diagonal sets, the board and the recursion each hold at most n entries, excluding the output. Space is O(n).

variables.n: board side, also number of queens

entries.title: Spiral Matrix
entries.whyTime: Each of the m·n cells is appended exactly once while four shrinking borders are walked. Time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: Only the four border indexes are stored, excluding the output, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Unique Paths
entries.whyTime: Each of the m·n cells gets its path count from its top and left neighbours in O(1). Time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: Only one row of n counts is kept and updated in place, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Add Binary
entries.whyTime: Walking both strings from the right, each step adds one digit from each plus the carry. The loop runs about max(m, n) times at O(1) each, so time is O(max(m, n)).
entries.whySpace: The result stores one digit per step, at most max(m, n) + 1 digits, so space is O(max(m, n)).

entries.title: Sqrt(x)
entries.whyTime: Binary search over the candidates from 0 to n halves the range each step, so there are about log n steps. Time is O(log n).
entries.whySpace: Only the low, high and mid values are stored, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Edit Distance
entries.whyTime: The DP table has (m + 1)·(n + 1) cells, each computed from its insert, delete and replace neighbours in O(1). Time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The table stores every cell, so space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Set Matrix Zeroes
entries.whyTime: One pass records zeros in the first row and column, and a second pass zeroes cells from those marks. Each pass touches m·n cells, so time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The first row and first column act as the markers, so only a couple of flags are extra and space is O(1).

entries.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II
entries.whyTime: A dummy head and one pointer walk the list once, skipping each run of equal values. Every node is visited once, so time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the dummy node and a few pointers are stored, relinking in place, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List
entries.whyTime: One pointer walks the list once, unlinking each node that repeats its predecessor's value. Every node is visited once, so time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only one pointer is stored, relinking in place, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Maximal Rectangle
entries.whyTime: Each row updates the column heights in O(n), then a monotonic stack finds the largest rectangle of that histogram in O(n). Over m rows, time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The heights array and the stack hold at most n entries each, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Partition List
entries.whyTime: One pass sends each node to the end of a less-than list or a greater-or-equal list. Every node is visited once, so time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The two lists reuse the existing nodes, with only two dummy heads and tails added, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Decode Ways
entries.whyTime: Each position is decoded from the one-digit and two-digit codes ending there, an O(1) check. One pass over the n characters is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The count at a position needs only the previous two counts, so two variables suffice and space is O(1).

entries.title: Reverse Linked List II
entries.whyTime: Walk to the node before the left position, then reverse the nodes up to the right position in one pass. At most n nodes are touched, so time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The reversal rewires next pointers in place with a few pointers, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal
entries.whyTime: Each node is pushed and popped once (or visited once by the recursion), and is added to the result in O(1). n nodes give O(n).
entries.whySpace: The stack holds the path of left ancestors, at most h nodes. Space is O(h), excluding the output.

entries.title: Interleaving String
entries.whyTime: The DP has one cell for each pair of a prefix of s1 and a prefix of s2, each filled in O(1) from two neighbours. m·n cells give O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: Each row of the table depends only on the row before, so one row of n+1 booleans over s2 is kept. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal
entries.whyTime: A hash map from value to inorder index makes each root's split point an O(1) lookup. Each of the n nodes is built once from the postorder, so time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The map stores one index per node, n entries, and the recursion is at most h frames deep. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Minimum Depth of Binary Tree
entries.whyTime: The DFS visits each node once and, at a node with one child, follows only that child. Worst case it visits all n nodes in O(1) each, so O(n).
entries.whySpace: The recursion depth equals the tree's height, one frame per level on the current path. Space is O(h).

entries.title: Distinct Subsequences
entries.whyTime: For each of the m characters of s, the DP updates one count for each of the n prefixes of t in O(1). m·n updates give O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: Only one array of n+1 counts over the prefixes of t is kept and updated as s is scanned. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers
entries.whyTime: Each node is visited once, extending the number built so far in O(1) and adding it to the total at a leaf. n nodes give O(n).
entries.whySpace: The recursion depth equals the tree's height, one frame per level on the current path. Space is O(h).

entries.title: Single Number
entries.whyTime: One pass XORs all n numbers together. Pairs cancel out, leaving the single number, and each XOR is O(1). Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: A single integer holds the running XOR. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Word Break
entries.whyTime: For each of the n positions of s, the DP compares each of the m words against s, an O(L) comparison. n·m·L work gives O(n·m·L).
entries.whySpace: A dp array of n+1 booleans, one per prefix of s, is the only table. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Word Break II
entries.whyTime: A string of length n has up to 2^(n−1) ways to place spaces, and each sentence takes O(n) to build. Memoizing by start index only avoids repeats, so time is O(n·2ⁿ).
entries.whySpace: The memo stores every sentence for every suffix of s, and in the worst case those lists hold O(n·2ⁿ) characters in all. Space is O(n·2ⁿ).

entries.title: Linked List Cycle II
entries.whyTime: Fast and slow pointers meet within about n steps. A second walk from the head and the meeting point finds the cycle start in at most n more. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the slow and fast pointers are kept, with no visited set. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Maximum Product Subarray
entries.whyTime: One pass over n numbers. Each step updates the running max and min product ending there in O(1), tracking both since a negative flips them. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the running max, running min and best product are kept. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Binary Search Tree Iterator
entries.whyTime: next() pops a node and pushes the left spine of its right child. Each node is pushed and popped once across all calls, so each call is amortized O(1). hasNext() is O(1).
entries.whySpace: The stack holds only the pending left ancestors of the current position, one path of at most h nodes. Space is O(h).

entries.title: Reverse Bits
entries.whyTime: The loop shifts one bit per iteration over a fixed 32-bit integer, so it runs 32 times whatever the value. Time is O(1).
entries.whySpace: Only the input and the result integer are kept. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Number of 1 Bits
entries.whyTime: The loop handles one bit (or clears one set bit) per iteration over a fixed 32-bit integer, so at most 32 iterations. Time is O(1).
entries.whySpace: Only n and a counter are kept. Space is O(1).

entries.title: House Robber
entries.whyTime: One pass over the n houses. At each house the best total is the larger of skipping it or robbing it plus the total two houses back, in O(1). Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: Each house needs only the best totals for the previous two houses, so two scalars suffice. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Count Primes
entries.whyTime: The sieve crosses off the multiples of each prime p below n, about n/p steps each. Summing n/p over primes p gives n log log n.
entries.whySpace: A boolean array of n entries marks which numbers below n are composite. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Isomorphic Strings
entries.whyTime: One pass over the n character pairs. Each of the two maps does an O(1) lookup and insert, so O(n).
entries.whySpace: Each map holds at most one entry per distinct ASCII character, a fixed alphabet that does not grow with n. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
entries.whyTime: The right pointer visits each of the n elements once, and the left pointer only moves forward. Together they take at most 2n steps, so O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the two pointers, the window sum and the best length are kept. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Word Search II
entries.whyTime: A DFS starts from each of the m·n cells and follows trie edges. It goes at most k letters deep and branches into at most 3 unvisited neighbours per step. Time is O(m·n·3^k), trie build excluded.
entries.whySpace: The trie stores up to W·k characters across the W words. The DFS adds at most k frames on top. Space is O(W·k).

entries.title: House Robber II
entries.whyTime: The first and last houses are neighbours, so run the linear House Robber twice, on nums[:-1] and on nums[1:]. Each run is one O(n) pass, so O(n).
entries.whySpace: Each run needs only two scalars for the best totals of the previous two houses. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
entries.whyTime: Each of the n elements is pushed onto a min-heap that is capped at k elements. A push or pop on a heap of size k is O(log k), so O(n log k).
entries.whySpace: The heap never holds more than k elements. Space is O(k).

variables.k: rank k of the kth largest

entries.title: The Skyline Problem
entries.whyTime: A sweep over the 2n edges pushes each building onto a max-heap once and pops it once. Each heap operation is O(log n), so O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The heap holds up to n buildings, and the skyline output holds up to 2n points. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Contains Duplicate III
entries.whyTime: Each of the n values maps to one bucket of width valueDiff+1. Checking its own and two neighbouring buckets, and evicting the oldest, are O(1) hash lookups. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: The bucket map holds one entry per element in the last k positions, never more than n. Space is O(min(n, k)).

entries.title: Maximal Square
entries.whyTime: The DP fills one cell for each of the m·n matrix cells, each from three neighbouring cells in O(1). Total O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: A cell depends only on the row above and the cell to its left, so one row of n+1 values is kept. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Basic Calculator
entries.whyTime: One pass over the n characters. Each digit, sign or parenthesis is handled with O(1) stack work. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: The stack saves the running result and sign at each open parenthesis. Nesting can reach about n/2 levels, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
entries.whyTime: Iterative in-order walks down to the leftmost node in h steps, then pops k nodes in order and stops at the kth. Each pop is amortized O(1), so O(h + k).
entries.whySpace: The stack holds the path of pending left ancestors, at most h nodes. Space is O(h).

entries.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
entries.whyTime: push appends to the input stack in O(1). pop and peek move everything to the output stack only when it is empty, so each element moves once: amortized O(1) per operation.
entries.whySpace: Every element sits in exactly one of the two stacks, so n elements use O(n).

entries.title: Number of Digit One
entries.whyTime: The loop handles one decimal digit per step and counts that digit's ones with arithmetic. n has about log n digits: O(log n).
entries.whySpace: Only a few integer variables are kept: O(1).

entries.title: Palindrome Linked List
entries.whyTime: Slow and fast pointers find the middle in about n / 2 steps, the second half is reversed in n / 2, and both halves are compared in n / 2: O(n).
entries.whySpace: The second half is reversed in place by relinking next pointers, with only a few pointers kept: O(1).

entries.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
entries.whyTime: The recursion visits each node at most once, reporting whether p or q lies below it: O(n).
entries.whySpace: The call stack goes as deep as the tree is tall: O(h).

entries.title: Meeting Rooms
entries.whyTime: Sorting by start time costs O(n log n). One pass then checks each meeting starts after the previous one ends, so the sort dominates: O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The sort is in place and the pass compares neighbours with no extra structure: O(1).

entries.title: Meeting Rooms II
entries.whyTime: Sorting by start is O(n log n). Each meeting does one push and at most one pop on the end-time heap, O(log n) each: O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The heap holds the end time of every room in use, up to n when all meetings overlap: O(n).

entries.title: Missing Number
entries.whyTime: One pass XORs every index and every value into a running total, which leaves the missing number: O(n).
entries.whySpace: A single integer accumulator is kept: O(1).

entries.title: First Bad Version
entries.whyTime: Binary search halves the range of versions with each isBadVersion call: O(log n).
entries.whySpace: Only the low, high and mid indices are kept: O(1).

entries.title: Walls and Gates
entries.whyTime: A multi-source BFS starts from all gates at once. Each room is enqueued at most once and checks 4 neighbours: O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The queue can hold every room, for example a grid full of gates: O(m·n).

entries.title: Find the Duplicate Number
entries.whyTime: Floyd's cycle detection treats each value as a next pointer. The slow and fast pointers meet in O(n) steps and the walk to the cycle entrance is another O(n): O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only two pointers are kept and nums is never modified: O(1).

entries.title: Find Median from Data Stream
entries.whyTime: addNum pushes onto one of two heaps and may move one element to rebalance, each O(log n). findMedian only reads the heap tops in O(1), so the cost per addNum is O(log n).
entries.whySpace: The two heaps together hold every number added: O(n).

entries.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
entries.whyTime: Serialize visits each node once in preorder and deserialize rebuilds each node once from the tokens: O(n).
entries.whySpace: The serialized tokens hold one value per node plus null markers, at most 2n + 1 tokens: O(n).

entries.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (O(n log n))
entries.whyTime: Each number is placed into the sorted tails array with a binary search of O(log n). n numbers give O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The tails array holds up to n entries when nums is strictly increasing: O(n).

entries.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
entries.whyTime: The O(n) prefix-sum build runs once in the constructor. Each sumRange subtracts two prefix entries, so a query is O(1).
entries.whySpace: The prefix array stores n + 1 running sums: O(n).

entries.whySpace: The prefix matrix stores one running sum per cell: O(m·n).

entries.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
entries.whyTime: One pass over the days updates the hold, sold and rest states from the previous day in O(1) each: O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the three states from the previous day are kept: O(1).

entries.title: Minimum Height Trees
entries.whyTime: A tree has n - 1 edges. Building adjacency lists is O(n) and the leaf-trimming BFS removes each node once: O(n).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency lists, degree array and leaf queue each hold at most n entries: O(n).

entries.title: Burst Balloons
entries.whyTime: The interval DP has O(n²) (left, right) states. Each tries every balloon in between as the last to burst, O(n) per state: O(n³).
entries.whySpace: The table stores one value per (left, right) pair: O(n²).

entries.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
entries.whyTime: A merge sort over indices counts smaller elements as the right half is merged in. There are log n levels of O(n) work: O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The index array, the merge buffer and the counts each hold n entries: O(n).

entries.title: Coin Change
entries.whyTime: dp[a] is the fewest coins for amount a. Each of the n amounts tries all k coins: O(n·k).
entries.whySpace: The dp array holds one entry per amount from 0 to n: O(n).

entries.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
entries.whyTime: Memoized DFS computes each cell's longest path once and reuses it. Each computation checks 4 neighbours: O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The memo table has one entry per cell, and the recursion can go m·n deep on a snaking path: O(m·n).

entries.title: House Robber III
entries.whyTime: A post-order DFS visits each node once and returns its (robbed, skipped) pair in O(1): O(n).
entries.whySpace: No memo table is needed. The recursion stack is as deep as the tree is tall: O(h).

entries.title: Counting Bits
entries.whyTime: Each i sets bits[i] from bits[i >> 1] plus its last bit in O(1), so filling n + 1 entries is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The result array of n + 1 counts is also the DP table the loop reads back, so it counts: O(n).

entries.title: Russian Doll Envelopes
entries.whyTime: Sorting by width (ties by height descending) is O(n log n). The longest increasing subsequence over heights does one binary search per envelope: O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The tails array of heights holds up to n entries: O(n).

entries.title: Sum of Two Integers
entries.whyTime: The carry loop runs once per bit position and the 32-bit mask caps it at 32 iterations, a constant: O(1).
entries.whySpace: Only the sum and carry integers are kept: O(1).

entries.title: Combination Sum IV
entries.whyTime: dp[t] counts ordered ways to reach total t. Each of the n totals tries all k numbers: O(n·k).
entries.whySpace: The dp array holds one count per total from 0 to n: O(n).

entries.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
entries.whyTime: insert appends to a list and records the index in a map. remove swaps with the last item and pops. getRandom indexes the list. Every operation is O(1) on average.
entries.whySpace: The list and the index map each hold n values: O(n).

entries.title: Linked List Random Node
entries.whyTime: Reservoir sampling walks the whole list on each getRandom, keeping node i with probability 1 / i: O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the chosen value and a counter are kept, with nothing copied from the list: O(1).

entries.title: Ransom Note
entries.whyTime: Count the letters of magazine in O(n), then spend them while scanning ransomNote in O(m): O(n + m).
entries.whySpace: The count holds at most 26 lowercase letters: O(1).

entries.title: Decode String
entries.whyTime: Each input character is pushed or popped once, and repeating a segment copies it into the output, so the work follows the output length: O(n).
entries.whySpace: The stack holds partial strings and counts for the open brackets, at most the size of the decoded output: O(n).

entries.title: Longest Palindrome
entries.whyTime: One pass counts each letter, then at most 52 counts are summed: O(n).
entries.whySpace: The count map holds at most 52 keys (upper and lower case letters): O(1).

entries.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
entries.whyTime: A 1D boolean DP marks which sums up to k are reachable. Each of the n numbers updates all k sums: O(n·k).
entries.whySpace: One boolean per sum from 0 to k: O(k).

entries.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers
entries.whyTime: Each number is inserted into a bit trie 32 levels deep and queried 32 levels deep. The fixed width makes each number O(1): O(n).
entries.whySpace: The trie holds at most 32 nodes per number, a constant each: O(n).

entries.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
entries.whyTime: Counting the letters of p costs O(m). A fixed-size window then slides over s, updating one letter count and comparing 26 counts per step: O(n + m).
entries.whySpace: Two 26-slot count arrays are kept, excluding the output list: O(1).

entries.title: Repeated Substring Pattern
entries.whyTime: A KMP failure table is built in one O(n) pass. s repeats when n is divisible by the period n - fail[n - 1], an O(1) check: O(n).
entries.whySpace: The failure table has one entry per character: O(n).

entries.title: LFU Cache
entries.whyTime: A key map and ordered frequency buckets give O(1) lookup, O(1) move of a key to the next frequency and O(1) eviction of the oldest key at the minimum frequency: O(1) per get and put.
entries.whySpace: At most k keys are stored across the maps, plus one bucket per frequency in use: O(k).

entries.title: Reverse Pairs
entries.whyTime: Merge sort has log n levels. At each merge two pointers count pairs with nums[i] > 2·nums[j] in O(n): O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The merge buffer holds up to n values: O(n).

entries.title: Target Sum
entries.whyTime: Counting subsets that reach a derived target of at most k is a DP over sums. Each of the n numbers updates up to k sums: O(n·k).
entries.whySpace: A 1D DP array holds one count per sum up to k: O(k).

entries.title: Fibonacci
entries.whyTime: A loop adds the previous two values n times, O(1) per step: O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the last two values are kept: O(1).

entries.title: Find Largest Value in Each Tree Row
entries.whyTime: BFS visits each node once and keeps the maximum of each level: O(n).
entries.whySpace: The queue holds a whole level, up to about n / 2 nodes in a wide tree: O(n).

entries.title: Coin Change II
entries.whyTime: For each of the k coins, dp is updated across all n amounts, with coins in the outer loop so orderings are not double counted: O(n·k).
entries.whySpace: The dp array holds one count per amount from 0 to n: O(n).

entries.title: Contiguous Array
entries.whyTime: One pass over n elements, treating 0 as -1 and tracking the running sum. Each hash map lookup and insert is O(1), so the loop is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The map stores the first index of each distinct running sum, up to n + 1 entries. Space is O(n).

entries.title: 01 Matrix
entries.whyTime: Multi-source BFS starts from every 0 and enqueues each cell at most once. Each of the m·n cells does 4 neighbor checks, so the total is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The queue and the distance matrix can hold up to m·n cells. Space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Number of Provinces
entries.whyTime: Each city is visited once, and visiting it scans its full row of n entries in isConnected. That is n rows of n cells, so O(n²).
entries.whySpace: The visited array holds n flags and the DFS stack can be n deep. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Erect the Fence
entries.whyTime: Sorting the n points costs O(n log n). Building the lower and upper hulls with a monotone chain pushes and pops each point a constant number of times, O(n). The sort dominates: O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The sorted copy and the two hull stacks hold up to n points. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Merge Two Binary Trees
entries.whyTime: Both trees are walked in step, and recursion stops where either node is missing, reusing the other subtree as is. At most n overlapping pairs give O(n).
entries.whySpace: The recursion follows one root-to-node path of both trees, so the stack is at most h frames deep. Space is O(h).

entries.title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
entries.whyTime: BFS dequeues each of the n nodes once and adds its value to its level sum. Per-node work is O(1), so the total is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The queue holds one whole level at a time, up to about n/2 nodes in a wide tree. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Maximum Average Subarray I
entries.whyTime: Sum the first k values, then slide the window one step at a time: add the new element and drop the old one. That is n steps of O(1) work, so O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the running window sum and the best sum are stored. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Maximum Length of Pair Chain
entries.whyTime: Sorting the pairs by end value costs O(n log n). The greedy scan then looks at each pair once, O(n). The sort dominates: O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The sort uses an O(n) temporary buffer and the scan keeps only the last chosen end. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Palindromic Substrings
entries.whyTime: There are 2n - 1 centers. Expanding outward from each center can run up to n/2 steps of O(1) each, so the total is O(n²).
entries.whySpace: Only the center, the two expanding pointers and the counter are stored. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Valid Parenthesis String
entries.whyTime: One pass over s tracks the lowest and highest possible count of open parentheses, treating * as ( or ) or empty. O(1) work per character gives O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the two counters lo and hi are stored. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
entries.whyTime: Bitmask DP over the 2ⁿ subsets of nums. For each mask, try adding each of the n unused elements. That is n work per mask, so O(n·2ⁿ).
entries.whySpace: The DP table stores one running sum per mask, 2ⁿ entries. Space is O(2ⁿ).

entries.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
entries.whyTime: Each step takes dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). That is n steps of O(1) work, so O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the two previous dp values are kept, not the full table. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Cracking the Safe
entries.whyTime: Hierholzer's DFS walks each of the kⁿ edges of the de Bruijn graph once, building a length-n string for each edge. That is kⁿ steps of O(n) work, so O(n·kⁿ).
entries.whySpace: The visited set stores up to kⁿ strings of length n, and the answer has about kⁿ + n - 1 digits. Space is O(n·kⁿ).

variables.k: number of digit values (0 to k-1)

entries.title: Find Eventual Safe States
entries.whyTime: Topological sort on the reversed graph: each node enters the queue once and each edge is decremented once. Total O(V + E).
entries.whySpace: The reversed adjacency lists hold E edges; the out-degree counts and the queue hold V nodes. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: Bricks Falling When Hit
entries.whyTime: Remove all hit bricks, union the m·n cells, then add the k hits back in reverse, each with at most 4 unions. Hits are unique, so k ≤ m·n, and union-find costs near O(1) per step. Time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: Union-find keeps a parent and a size per cell plus one roof node, and a copy of the grid is kept. Space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Bus Routes
entries.whyTime: Building the stop-to-buses map reads every stop once. BFS visits each bus once and scans each stop's bus list once, so every stop entry is touched a constant number of times. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: The stop-to-buses map has one entry per stop of every route, n in total. The visited sets hold at most n stops and m buses. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Most Common Word
entries.whyTime: Lowercasing and splitting the paragraph is O(n), and counting each word is an O(1) hash update. Building the banned set takes O(m) because each word has at most 10 letters. Total O(n + m).
entries.whySpace: The word counter holds up to n words and the banned set holds m. Space is O(n + m).

entries.title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
entries.whyTime: BFS over states (node, visited mask) has n·2ⁿ states. Each state tries every neighbor, so a mask is expanded across all edges: about 2E·2ⁿ ≤ n²·2ⁿ transitions. Total O(n²·2ⁿ).
entries.whySpace: The visited set and the queue hold up to n·2ⁿ states. Space is O(n·2ⁿ).

entries.title: Middle of the Linked List
entries.whyTime: fast moves two nodes per step and slow moves one, so fast reaches the end after about n/2 steps. That is O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the slow and fast pointers are stored. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Smallest Range II
entries.whyTime: Sort nums in O(n log n). One scan then tries each split point, giving the first i elements +k and the rest -k, with O(1) work each. The sort dominates: O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The sort uses an O(n) temporary buffer and the scan keeps only a few scalars. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Binary Tree Cameras
entries.whyTime: Post-order DFS visits each of the n nodes once and picks its state (covered, camera or needs cover) from its children in O(1). Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the recursion stack is used, as deep as the tree is tall. Space is O(h).

entries.title: Squares of a Sorted Array
entries.whyTime: Two pointers start at both ends. Each step writes the larger square into the next slot of the result from the back, so n steps of O(1) work give O(n).
entries.whySpace: The result list holds n squares. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
entries.whyTime: Timestamps in a key's list arrive in increasing order, so set is an O(1) append. get binary-searches that sorted list of up to n entries, so it costs O(log n).
entries.whySpace: Every set call stores one (timestamp, value) entry. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Interval List Intersections
entries.whyTime: Two pointers walk both lists, and each step advances the pointer whose interval ends first. At most n + m steps of O(1) work, so O(n + m).
entries.whySpace: The result holds at most n + m - 1 intersections. Space is O(n + m).

entries.title: Minimum Cost to Merge Stones
entries.whyTime: Interval DP over n piles. Each of the O(n²) intervals tries splits every k - 1 piles, about n/k split points, with O(1) work each. Total O(n³/k).
entries.whySpace: dp is an n × n table of minimum costs, plus prefix sums. Space is O(n²).

entries.title: Stream of Characters
entries.whyTime: A trie holds the reversed words. Each query walks the trie from the newest letter backward and stops at a miss or after the longest word, at most L steps of O(1). A query is O(L).
entries.whySpace: The trie stores each of the n words reversed, up to L nodes each. Space is O(n·L).

entries.title: Robot Bounded In Circle
entries.whyTime: Run the instructions once, updating position and direction in O(1) per character. The robot is bounded if it ends at the origin or not facing north. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the x, y and direction values are stored. Space is O(1).

entries.title: Longest Duplicate Substring
entries.whyTime: Binary search on the substring length takes O(log n) rounds. Each round slides a rolling hash over s in O(n) and checks a set of hashes. Total O(n log n) expected.
entries.whySpace: Each round stores up to n hashes in a set. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Path With Maximum Minimum Value
entries.whyTime: A max-heap Dijkstra pops each of the m·n cells once and pushes its neighbors. Each heap operation is O(log(m·n)), so the total is O(m·n log(m·n)).
entries.whySpace: The heap and the visited set hold up to m·n cells. Space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Corporate Flight Bookings
entries.whyTime: Each booking adds seats at first and subtracts after last in a difference array, O(1) per booking, so O(m). One prefix-sum pass over the n flights adds O(n). Total O(n + m).
entries.whySpace: The answer array has one slot per flight. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Connecting Cities With Minimum Cost
entries.whyTime: Kruskal's sorts the E connections in O(E log E). Union-find then handles each edge in near-constant time, so the sort dominates: O(E log E).
entries.whySpace: The sorted edge list holds E entries and union-find holds V parents. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: Longest Common Subsequence
entries.whyTime: The DP table has a cell for each pair of prefixes, (m + 1)·(n + 1) cells, and each is filled in O(1) from three neighbors. Total O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The full table stores m·n cells. Space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Online Majority Element in Subarray
entries.whyTime: A segment tree of Boyer-Moore candidates answers a range in O(log n). Confirming the candidate counts its positions with two binary searches, also O(log n). A query is O(log n).
entries.whySpace: The segment tree holds about 2n nodes and the position lists hold n indices. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Invalid Transactions
entries.whyTime: Each transaction is compared with every other one for the same name, a different city and a time within 60 minutes. That is n × n pairs of O(1) checks, so O(n²).
entries.whySpace: The parsed transactions and the invalid flags hold n entries. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Critical Connections
entries.whyTime: Tarjan's DFS visits each server once and each connection twice (once per direction), updating discovery and low-link times in O(1). Total O(V + E).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency lists hold E connections, the discovery and low arrays hold V entries, and the recursion goes up to V deep. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: Minimum Knight Moves
entries.whyTime: BFS from the origin uses symmetry to search one quadrant plus a small margin. It visits cells within about n of the origin in each direction, O(1) work each. Total O(n²).
entries.whySpace: The visited set and the queue hold those same cells. Space is O(n²).

entries.title: Smallest String With Swaps
entries.whyTime: Union-find merges the m pairs at near-constant cost each, O(m·α(n)). Each connected group's characters are then sorted, and all groups together hold n characters: O(n log n). Total O(n log n + m·α(n)).
entries.whySpace: The union-find arrays and the per-group character lists hold n entries in total, excluding the pairs input. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
entries.whyTime: Sorting the n jobs by end time costs O(n log n). Each job then does one binary search over earlier end times, O(log n), for n·log n more. Total O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The sorted jobs and the dp array hold one entry per job, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
entries.whyTime: One pass pushes the index of each '(' on a stack and flags unmatched ')'. A second pass rebuilds the string. Every character is handled a constant number of times, so O(n).
entries.whySpace: The index stack, the set of removed indices and the rebuilt character list each hold at most n entries, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Search Suggestions System
entries.whyTime: Sorting the n products costs O(n log n) comparisons of up to L characters each. Each of the m typed prefixes then does a binary search of O(log n) such comparisons. Total O((n + m)·L log n).
entries.whySpace: The sorted copy of products holds n references; the suggestion lists are the output and are excluded. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Maximum Students Taking Exam
entries.whyTime: Each of the m rows tries every pair of column masks, previous row and current row, 2ⁿ × 2ⁿ = 4ⁿ pairs, each checked with O(1) bit operations. Total O(m·4ⁿ).
entries.whySpace: The DP table is indexed by the 2ⁿ masks of the previous row and is rolled forward row by row, so space is O(2ⁿ).

entries.title: Minimum Cost to Make at Least One Valid Path in a Grid
entries.whyTime: 0-1 BFS over the m·n cells: following a cell's own arrow costs 0 (front of the deque), changing it costs 1 (back). Each cell is settled once with four neighbor checks, so O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The cost grid holds m·n entries and the deque holds O(m·n) cells, so space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Check if There is a Valid Path in a Grid
entries.whyTime: BFS from (0, 0) visits each of the m·n cells at most once, checking its two street openings in O(1). Total O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The visited set and the BFS queue hold up to m·n cells, so space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Design Underground System
entries.note: per call
entries.whyTime: checkIn, checkOut and getAverageTime each do a constant number of hash map lookups and updates, with no loop over the stored data, so each call is O(1).
entries.whySpace: One map holds each rider currently checked in, another holds a running total and count per station pair. Both grow at most with the n calls, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Minimum Time to Collect All Apples in a Tree
entries.whyTime: A DFS from vertex 0 visits each of the n vertices once and each of the n − 1 edges twice. A subtree costs 2 seconds when it holds an apple, so time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency list stores the n − 1 edges, and the recursion can be n frames deep on a path-shaped tree. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Design Browser History
entries.note: per call
entries.whyTime: History is an array with a current pointer and an end pointer. visit writes one slot and moves the end; back and forward move the pointer by a clamped amount. Each call is O(1).
entries.whySpace: The array holds every visited url that has not been overwritten, at most n, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Kth Ancestor of a Tree Node
entries.note: per query; build is O(n log n)
entries.whyTime: Binary lifting stores every node's 2^j-th ancestors. A query makes one jump per set bit of k, at most log k jumps, each an O(1) table lookup: O(log k).
entries.whySpace: The lifting table has one row per node (n) and about log n levels of 2^j-th ancestors, so space is O(n log n).

entries.title: Count Submatrices With All Ones
entries.whyTime: Row by row, update each column's run of consecutive ones. A monotonic stack over those heights counts every submatrix ending in that row in amortized O(n). All m rows give O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The heights array, the monotonic stack and the per-column counts each hold n entries, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Path with Maximum Probability
entries.whyTime: Dijkstra with a max-heap on success probability. Each of the E edges can push one heap entry costing O(log E) = O(log V), so the total is O(E log V).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency list holds 2E entries, the probability array V, and the heap up to E. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: Best Position for a Service Centre
entries.whyTime: Nested ternary search over x then y runs a fixed number of iterations for the required precision. Each evaluation sums the distances to the n customers, so the total is O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the search bounds and a running sum are kept, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Minimum Cost to Cut a Stick
entries.whyTime: Sort the cuts and add both ends. Interval DP has about k² (i, j) states, and each tries up to k split points, so the total is O(k³).
entries.whySpace: The DP table has one entry per pair of cut positions, about k² entries, so space is O(k²).

entries.title: Minimum Number of Vertices to Reach All Nodes
entries.whyTime: One pass over the E edges marks every node that has an incoming edge, then one pass over the V nodes collects the unmarked ones. Total O(V + E).
entries.whySpace: One flag per node marks incoming edges, excluding the output list. Space is O(V).

entries.title: Throne Inheritance
entries.whyTime: birth and death are O(1) each, a list append and a set insert. getInheritanceOrder runs a preorder DFS that visits each of the n people once, so it is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The children lists store one entry per person and the dead set holds at most n names. The DFS stack is at most n deep. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Number of Ways to Form a Target String Given a Dictionary
entries.whyTime: Each of the n columns counts its characters over the W words, m steps in all. The DP then updates k target positions per column, n·k steps. Time is O(m + n·k).
entries.whySpace: Only a 26-entry letter count and one DP array over the k target positions are kept. Space is O(k).

entries.title: Count the Number of Consistent Strings
entries.whyTime: Building the allowed set reads m characters. Each of the n words is then checked one character at a time against it in O(1) per character, at most L each. Total O(n·L + m).
entries.whySpace: The allowed set holds its m characters, so space is O(m).

entries.title: Count Good Meals
entries.whyTime: For each of the n foods, try every power of two up to twice the largest value, about log m of them, and look up the partner count in a hash map in O(1). Total O(n log m).
entries.whySpace: The count map holds each distinct value, at most n entries, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Ways to Split Array Into Three Subarrays
entries.whyTime: Prefix sums take one pass. For each end of the left part, the lowest and highest valid ends of the middle part only move forward, so each index is passed a constant number of times. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: The prefix sum array holds n + 1 entries, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Restore the Array From Adjacent Pairs
entries.whyTime: One pass over the n - 1 pairs builds the neighbor map, one scan finds an end value with a single neighbor, and one walk along the chain visits each value once. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: The neighbor map holds 2(n - 1) entries and the rebuilt array holds n values, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Closest Subsequence Sum
entries.whyTime: Split nums into two halves of n/2. Each half yields 2^(n/2) subset sums, sorted at O(n·2^(n/2)). A two-pointer sweep then pairs sums across halves in O(2^(n/2)). Total O(n·2^(n/2)).
entries.whySpace: The two lists of subset sums hold 2^(n/2) entries each, so space is O(2^(n/2)).

entries.title: Number of Orders in the Backlog
entries.whyTime: Each matching step either empties a heap top or finishes the batch, so there are O(n) heap operations in all, each O(log n). Total O(n log n).
entries.whySpace: The buy and sell heaps together hold at most one entry per batch, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Maximum Number of Accepted Invitations
entries.whyTime: Kuhn's matching starts one DFS per boy. Each DFS visits every girl at most once and scans each invitation at most once, O(E). With at most V starts the total is O(V·E).
entries.whySpace: The girl-to-boy match array, the visited array and the DFS recursion each hold at most V entries, so space is O(V).

entries.title: Minimum Interval to Include Each Query

entries.whyTime: Sorting the intervals costs O(n log n) and sorting the queries O(q log q). The sweep pushes each interval into a min-heap once and pops it at most once, O(n log n). Total O(n log n + q log q).
entries.whySpace: The heap holds up to n intervals, and the sorted queries and the answer array hold q entries each. Space is O(n + q).

entries.title: Rotating the Box
entries.whyTime: Each row is scanned once to drop its stones, then every cell is copied into the rotated grid. Both steps touch the m·n cells a constant number of times: O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The rotated n by m result stores m·n cells, the output itself counted, so space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Minimum Number of Flips to Make the Binary String Alternating
entries.whyTime: Slide a window of length n over s + s, flipping the counts against both alternating patterns by one character in and one out per step. 2n steps of O(1) give O(n).
entries.whySpace: The doubled string s + s stores 2n characters. Space is O(n).

entries.title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
entries.whyTime: One pass over the n triplets skips any with a value above the target and otherwise records which target positions it matches, in O(1) each. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only three flags are kept, one per target position, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination
entries.whyTime: Dijkstra pushes at most one heap entry per relaxed road, O(E) entries at O(log E) = O(log V) each. The path counts update in O(1) per relaxation, so the total is O(E log V).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency list holds 2E entries, the distance and ways arrays V each, and the heap up to E. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: The Number of Good Subsets
entries.whyTime: One pass over nums counts how often each value from 1 to 30 occurs, O(n). The DP over prime-factor masks then runs on a fixed set of values and masks, independent of n. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: A count array for 30 values and a DP array over a fixed set of prime masks are both fixed size, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Detect Squares
entries.note: per count call; add is O(1)
entries.whyTime: add is one hash map increment. count tries every distinct stored point as the diagonal corner and looks up the other two corners in O(1) each, so a count call is O(n).
entries.whySpace: A map from each point to its multiplicity holds at most n entries, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Parallel Courses III
entries.whyTime: Kahn's topological order queues each course once and relaxes each relation once to update finish times. Total O(V + E).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency list holds E entries; the indegree, finish-time arrays and the queue hold V entries. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: Step-By-Step Directions From a Binary Tree Node to Another
entries.whyTime: One DFS finds the root-to-start path and another finds the root-to-destination path, each visiting at most n nodes. Trimming their common prefix is O(h), so time is O(n).
entries.whySpace: Each path holds at most h letters, and the recursion is at most h frames deep. Space is O(h).

entries.title: Find All Possible Recipes from Given Supplies
entries.whyTime: Kahn's algorithm: each ingredient listing adds one edge (E), each name is dequeued once (V), and each edge is processed once when its ingredient becomes available. Total O(V + E).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency map holds E entries, and the indegree map and the queue hold up to V entries. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: Calculate Amount Paid in Taxes
entries.whyTime: One pass over the n brackets taxes the slice of income inside each bracket in O(1) and stops once income is covered. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only a running tax total and the previous upper bound are kept, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Number of Increasing Paths in a Grid
entries.whyTime: A memoized DFS counts the increasing paths starting at each cell, checking 4 neighbors. Each of the m·n cells is computed once in O(1), so time is O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The memo stores one count per cell, and the recursion can be m·n frames deep along an increasing path. Space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Design SQL
entries.note: per ins, rmv, sel call; exp is O(n·k)
entries.whyTime: ins writes one row under its auto-increment id, rmv deletes one row by id, and sel looks up a table, row id and column. Each is a constant number of hash lookups, so O(1) per call.
entries.whySpace: Every stored row keeps up to k cells (n·k in all), and each of the m tables keeps a name entry and an id counter. Space is O(m + n·k).

entries.title: Minimum Penalty for a Shop
entries.whyTime: One pass over customers moves the closing hour right one step at a time: +1 penalty for an 'N' hour kept open, -1 for a 'Y'. It tracks the lowest penalty and earliest hour. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: Only the running penalty, the best penalty and the best hour are kept, so space is O(1).

entries.title: Collect Coins in a Tree
entries.whyTime: A queue of leaves trims coin-free leaves, then two more layers of leaves. Each node and edge is removed at most once, then the remaining edges are counted. Total O(n).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency list, the degree array and the leaf queue each hold O(n) entries, so space is O(n).

variables.n: number of nodes in the tree

entries.title: Minimum Cost of a Path With Special Roads
entries.whyTime: Dijkstra over the 2n + 2 points (start, target and both ends of every road). Each round scans all points to pick the closest unsettled one, then relaxes against all points. Total O(n²).
entries.whySpace: A distance value and a settled flag per point hold 2n + 2 entries, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Modify Graph Edge Weights
entries.whyTime: Two Dijkstra runs: one with unknown (-1) edges at weight 1, one that raises them as needed. Each run relaxes E edges through a heap at O(log V) each, so the total is O(E log V).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency list holds 2E entries, the distance arrays V, and the heap up to E. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: Minimum Edge Weight Equilibrium Queries in a Tree
entries.whyTime: Build the binary-lifting tables, each jump carrying counts for the 26 possible weights, in O(n log n). Each of the m queries finds the LCA and reads counts in O(log n). Total O((n + m) log n).
entries.whySpace: The tables hold n nodes by about log n jumps, each with 26 weight counts, so space is O(n log n).

variables.n: number of nodes in the tree

entries.title: Find Beautiful Indices in the Given Array II
entries.whyTime: KMP finds every match of a and of b in s in O(n + m). A two-pointer sweep over the two sorted match lists, checking the distance against k, passes each match once, O(n). Total O(n + m).
entries.whySpace: The KMP failure tables hold O(m) entries and the match lists hold up to n indices, excluding the output. Space is O(n + m).

variables.m: combined length of a and b

entries.title: Split the Array
entries.whyTime: One pass counts each value; if any value appears more than twice, no split exists. Each count update is O(1), so the total is O(n).
entries.whySpace: The count map holds each distinct value, at most n entries, so space is O(n).

entries.title: Minimum Operations to Write the Letter Y on a Grid
entries.whyTime: One pass over the n² cells tallies the values on the Y and off it. A fixed 3 by 3 check of value pairs then picks the cheapest recolouring. Total O(n²).
entries.whySpace: Two arrays of three counts are kept, which is constant size, so space is O(1).

variables.n: rows and columns of grid (n by n)

entries.title: Length of Longest V-Shaped Diagonal Segment
entries.whyTime: A memoised DFS over (cell, direction, turn used) states. There are a fixed number of directions and turn flags per cell, each state doing O(1) work over the m·n cells: O(m·n).
entries.whySpace: The memo table holds a fixed number of states per cell, m·n cells, and the recursion is at most O(m + n) deep. Space is O(m·n).

entries.title: Minimum Cost Path with Edge Reversals
entries.whyTime: Dijkstra on a graph where each of the E edges also offers a reversed move at twice the cost, 2E relaxations in all. Each push costs O(log E) = O(log V), so the total is O(E log V).
entries.whySpace: The adjacency list holds 2E entries, the distance array V, and the heap up to 2E. Space is O(V + E).

entries.title: Arbitrage
entries.whyTime: Take -log of each rate, so an arbitrage is a negative cycle. Bellman-Ford runs V rounds over all E rates, then one more round to detect any improvement. Total O(V·E).
entries.whySpace: One distance value per currency is kept, excluding the rates input. Space is O(V).

entries.title: Island Hopping
entries.whyTime: Prim's on the complete graph runs n rounds. Each round picks the nearest unconnected island in O(n) and updates the distances to the rest in O(n), so the total is O(n²).
entries.whySpace: A nearest-distance value and a connected flag per island are kept, so space is O(n).
